summary: Twelve comment-endorsed tools, learning resources, media, software, and a poetry collection from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 12 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: TrainScanner
items.source_story_title: MUNI Heritage Weekend in San Francisco
items.summary: An app that turns ordinary train videos into detailed line-scan photographs.
items.why_included: A commenter directly recommended it and highlighted the detailed results from regular cameras.
items.evidence: The commenter recommended TrainScanner for making line-scan images with an ordinary phone or camera.

evidence_sources.author: dllu
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you want to use a regular phone or camera, check out TrainScanner!

items.name: Text classification with Python 3.14's zstd module
items.source_story_title: Can gzip be a language model?
items.summary: A practical tutorial on using compression for text classification in Python.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly pointed readers to this directly relevant worked example.
items.evidence: The commenter recommended the tutorial as a companion to the compression-based language-model discussion.

evidence_sources.author: networked
evidence_sources.excerpt: Check out "Text classification with Python 3.14's zstd module"

items.name: Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms
items.source_story_title: Can gzip be a language model?
items.summary: David MacKay's approachable textbook connecting information theory, inference, and learning.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended it as an introductory treatment of the thread's core ideas.
items.evidence: The commenter said MacKay's textbook is worth reading for an introduction and broader applications.

evidence_sources.author: shoo
evidence_sources.excerpt: For anyone wanting an introductory text for information theory & that explores some of these connections & applications, it's worth checking out the late David MacKay's 2003 textbook Information Theory, Inference & Learning Algorithms

items.name: fail0verflow's PS3 hacking presentation
items.source_story_title: AMD's random number generator can't generate a 0?
items.summary: A console-hacking talk explaining the PlayStation 3's cryptographic failure story.
items.why_included: A commenter called the presentation great, informative, and entertaining.
items.evidence: The commenter praised the fail0verflow talk as a strong explanation of the underlying bug.

evidence_sources.author: lathiat
evidence_sources.excerpt: And for the full fail story behind it, fail0verflow hacking the PS3 presentation is great and covers the bug:

items.name: ShareCleaner
items.source_story_title: AI Has No Wisdom and Neither Will You
items.summary: An iOS utility that removes tracking parameters before links are shared.
items.why_included: An unaffiliated iOS user gave it a direct recommendation for mobile sharing.
items.evidence: The commenter recommends ShareCleaner for stripping trackers from links on iOS.

evidence_sources.author: toomuchtodo
evidence_sources.excerpt: I recommend https://sharecleaner.com/ for cleaning links of trackers when sharing from mobile. No affiliation, just a user on iOS.

items.name: Pi Memorisation
items.source_story_title: Engineering Memory: On learning to memorize first 100 digits of pi (2024)
items.summary: A mnemonic system for memorizing pi and recalling digits by position.
items.why_included: A user successfully applied the method to memorize and index sixty digits.
items.evidence: The commenter used the page's techniques and can recall sixty digits by place.

evidence_sources.author: KyleJune
evidence_sources.excerpt: I used the techniques described on this page to memorize pi. I've got 60 memorized where I can recall the digits by place.

items.name: Love Is a Dog from Hell
items.summary: Charles Bukowski's gritty poetry collection about love, loneliness, and vulnerability.
items.why_included: A longtime poetry buyer singled it out as a favorite Bukowski collection.
items.evidence: The commenter named Love Is a Dog from Hell as their favorite Bukowski poetry book.

evidence_sources.author: ggerules
evidence_sources.excerpt: My favorite Bukowski book of poetry "Love is a Dog from Hell". Very Bukowski.

items.name: Godot
items.source_story_title: First Shader from Zero in Godot 4
items.summary: An open-source game engine combining a compact workflow with broad capabilities.
items.why_included: Fresh praise framed Godot as powerful, delightful, and increasingly dominant for game jams.
items.evidence: The commenter praised Godot's simplicity and power and compared its game-jam momentum favorably with Unity.

evidence_sources.author: lemmetellya
evidence_sources.excerpt: Godot is such a delight. Brings me back to working with Flixel and Flash game dev. It's really shaping up to be a powerful tool in a simple package, and it's eating Unity's lunch for game jams these days.

items.name: Microsoft Access
items.source_story_title: Microsoft killed FoxPro in 2007. Anyway, here's FoxPro revived
items.summary: A Windows desktop database builder for forms, reports, and small applications.
items.why_included: A commenter strongly praised its niche between spreadsheets and larger database systems.
items.evidence: The commenter called Access very good and wished Linux and macOS had an equivalent.

evidence_sources.author: post-it
evidence_sources.excerpt: Access is so good. I can't believe there's no universal equivalent for Linux and Mac.

items.name: The Clicker
items.source_story_title: 9 Ads per Minute: FIFA Cup 26 – "the price of the beautiful game"
items.summary: An open-source device that mutes live ads and skips recorded commercials.
items.why_included: A commenter reported actively using it for automatic ad muting and skipping.
items.evidence: The commenter says the linked project automatically mutes live ads and skips recorded ones.

evidence_sources.author: gonzogato
evidence_sources.excerpt: I haven’t gotten to the “replace” bit yet, but I’m automatically muting live ads and auto skipping through recorded ones:

items.name: Innocuous
items.summary: A library for hiding steganographic signals in language-model output.
items.why_included: Its author reported a working implementation closely matching Anthropic's watermark approach.
items.evidence: The author says Innocuous implements LLM-output steganography and works with last year's llama.cpp.

evidence_sources.author: stillsut
evidence_sources.excerpt: I actually wrote a library to do stego with LLM outputs last year and it turned out to be an almost exact implementation of the Anthropic watermark algo.

items.name: pgdbf
items.source_story_title: Microsoft killed FoxPro in 2007. Anyway, here's FoxPro revived
items.summary: A command-line converter that loads Visual FoxPro DBF files into PostgreSQL.
items.why_included: Its author described successful production use during a legacy-system migration.
items.evidence: The author ran pgdbf on a schedule during migration and said it worked great.

evidence_sources.author: kstrauser
evidence_sources.excerpt: For a while we had to run it as a cron job so that people could to data entry in an old VFP app but others could run fast reports on our web app with a postgres backend. It wasn't pretty, but it worked great and helped us get off that ancient stack.
